blocks.text: Paramaribo, Peperpot and the river dolphins

provenance.rationale: Use the Paramaribo and Peperpot portion of the Word route heading for the Day 2 title.

blocks.text: A highlights tour of Paramaribo’s UNESCO-listed historic inner city, with its elegant Dutch colonial wooden buildings: Independence Square near the Presidential Palace, the Waterkant waterfront, the Palm Garden, Fort Zeelandia and the bustling Central Market. Then Peperpot Nature Park, a former coffee plantation reclaimed by the rainforest, with trails, tropical birds, monkeys and the historic plantation house. To finish, a river excursion on the Suriname River aboard a traditional tent boat to watch Guiana dolphins in the wild, before your driver takes you back from Leonsberg pier to the hotel. (B)

blocks.text: and 4. Upper Suriname River and Maroon culture

provenance.rationale: Compose the two-day route title from the Word Days 3–4 paragraph while retaining the continuation numbering.

blocks.text: Travel up the Upper Suriname River to a lodge on one of its many islands, to discover the culture of the Maroon communities, descendants of Africans who escaped slavery and preserved their traditions for generations. Visit their villages and meet the people, enjoy traditional dance and music, taste local cuisine made with ingredients from the forest and river, and listen to stories of their history and struggle for freedom. Take a “natural massage” in the rapids, go canoeing, hike the forest trails or simply relax by the river. Night 3 in a comfortable lodge with private bathroom; night 4 back at your hotel in Paramaribo. (2 breakfasts, 2 lunches, 1 dinner)
